videos.title: VoiceOver sigue abriendo puertas. Phonon trae nuevas voces a la conversación
videos.description:
VoiceOver continúa ampliando sus posibilidades, y hoy le toca el turno a Phonon, una aplicación que permite incorporar nuevas voces al lector de pantalla de Apple.
En este tutorial conoceremos cómo funciona Phonon, cómo explorar las voces disponibles, seleccionar las que nos interesan, descargarlas y utilizarlas con VoiceOver.
Todo explicado paso a paso, con demostraciones prácticas para que puedan escuchar las voces y valorar cuáles se ajustan mejor a sus preferencias.
Porque cuando hablamos de accesibilidad, tener más opciones para elegir siempre es una buena noticia.

videos.title: ¿Una galería de fotos pensada para personas ciegas? Así funciona Memora
videos.description:
Memora: ¿para qué quiere una persona ciega una galería de fotos?
¿Quién dijo que las fotografías son solamente para quienes pueden verlas?
Hoy les presento Memora, una aplicación para iPhone desarrollada por un programador ciego que propone una forma accesible de explorar y organizar nuestras fotografías.
En este tutorial recorreremos sus principales funciones, comprobaremos cómo se maneja con VoiceOver y veremos qué posibilidades ofrece en la práctica.
Una nueva oportunidad para demostrar que la accesibilidad también tiene mucho que decir en el mundo de la fotografía.
TifloAcosta. Tecnología al alcance de todos.

videos.title: Apple te quiere… proteger. ¡Pero tienes que activarlo! iOS 27
videos.description:
Apple quiere protegernos de las estafas, y con iOS 27 incorpora una nueva función llamada «Detección de riesgo de suplantación de identidad».
¿En qué consiste? ¿Puede nuestro iPhone detectar que alguien está intentando engañarnos para conseguir nuestro dinero o nuestros datos personales?
En este vídeo de TifloAcosta explico cómo funciona esta protección, cuáles son sus limitaciones y cómo podemos activarla desde los ajustes del iPhone utilizando VoiceOver.
Una novedad importante que viene desactivada de fábrica y que necesita aplicaciones compatibles para funcionar. No evita todas las estafas, pero puede aportar una protección adicional.

videos.title: Yo ya no persigo las noticias: ahora vienen a buscarme
videos.description:
En este vídeo les presento cMRSS, una aplicación accesible que permite reunir en un mismo lugar las fuentes de noticias y contenidos que realmente nos
interesan.
Podemos añadir medios y páginas mediante sus fuentes RSS, organizar lo que seguimos y consultar las novedades sin tener que ir saltando de una web a otra.
Pero hay una función que a mí me ha gustado especialmente: también podemos añadir canales de YouTube y seguir sus nuevas publicaciones desde la propia
aplicación, sin necesidad de entrar continuamente en YouTube para comprobar qué han publicado.
cMRSS no es gratuita, y eso también hay que decirlo. Pero después de usarla y comprobar lo que me ofrece, en mi caso considero que merece la pena la inversión.
En el vídeo les enseño cómo funciona, qué posibilidades ofrece y por qué se ha ganado un sitio entre las aplicaciones que utilizo para mantenerme informado.

videos.title: TifloAcosta ya tiene app: todo cambia a partir de aquí
videos.description:
TIFLOACOSTA APP — ACCESO DIRECTO
Este enlace abre directamente TifloAcosta App. No necesitas descargar ningún archivo ni registrarte para entrar. Desde ahí puedes utilizar la aplicación en el navegador y, si quieres, instalarla en tu dispositivo para tenerla disponible como una app más.
TifloAcosta da hoy uno de los pasos más importantes desde que comenzó este proyecto.
Durante mucho tiempo hemos ido creando vídeos, cursos, guías, documentos, recursos en español y en inglés y una comunidad que sigue creciendo. El problema es que todo ese material estaba repartido entre distintos lugares.
Ha llegado el momento de empezar a reunirlo.
TifloAcosta ya tiene su propia app.
Desde ella puedes buscar recursos por palabras, recorrerlos por categorías, consultar las novedades, guardar tus favoritos y acceder al catálogo completo de vídeos del Canal TifloAcosta.
Además, la aplicación se ha pensado desde el principio teniendo en cuenta la accesibilidad y el uso con lectores de pantalla.
En este vídeo te enseño cómo funciona, qué puedes encontrar dentro y cómo puedes instalarla para tener TifloAcosta mucho más cerca.
La demostración práctica se realiza en iPhone utilizando VoiceOver, y también explico cómo acceder e instalarla desde Android y Windows.
Si quieres entrar directamente mientras ves el vídeo, este es nuevamente el enlace:
La aplicación seguirá creciendo.
Iremos incorporando nuevos recursos, mejorando lo que ya existe y ajustando aquello que la experiencia real de los usuarios nos vaya indicando.
Porque esto no pretende ser simplemente otra página donde acumular enlaces.
La idea es mucho más ambiciosa: crear un lugar estable, accesible y sencillo desde el que entrar a todo lo que TifloAcosta va construyendo.
Hasta ahora, TifloAcosta era principalmente un canal, una comunidad y una colección de contenidos repartidos por distintos espacios.
Desde hoy empieza a tener su propia casa.
Y acabamos de abrir la puerta.

videos.title: Este atajo no pregunta, ve un código y se pone a investigar
videos.description:
Ponle un código delante… y a ver qué pasa
Hoy les traigo uno de esos atajos que empiezas haciendo para resolver una cosa y al final termina haciendo bastante más de lo previsto.
La idea es sencilla: encontrar un código y averiguar qué contiene.
Puede trabajar con códigos que estén en una imagen o una captura guardada en el iPhone, pero también con códigos que tengamos delante y podamos captar con la cámara.
Y no nos quedamos únicamente con los códigos QR.
El atajo también puede reconocer códigos de barras y, cuando encuentra información que merece la pena investigar, utiliza Internet para intentar averiguar qué hay detrás de ese código y ofrecernos información útil.
Por ejemplo, podemos encontrarnos un código de barras en un producto y querer saber qué es, o recibir una imagen que contiene un QR sin tener otro teléfono disponible para escanearlo.
La intención ha sido precisamente esa: tener una herramienta sencilla y accesible que podamos lanzar desde el iPhone y dejar que haga el trabajo.
En el vídeo les enseño cómo funciona y las distintas posibilidades que ofrece.
IMPORTANTE:
Para utilizar este atajo es necesario tener instalada la aplicación gratuita Actions, ya que algunas de las funciones que utiliza el atajo proceden de esta aplicación.
Descargar Actions desde la App Store:
Instalar el atajo:
Una vez instalada Actions, conviene abrirla al menos una vez. Si sus acciones no aparecen posteriormente en la aplicación Atajos, reinicien el iPhone.
Como siempre, este atajo lo comparto para que puedan probarlo, jugar con él y, sobre todo, sacarle partido.
Tony Acosta
Canal TifloAcosta

videos.title: Actualizaciones invisibles en iPhone: qué son y por qué importan
videos.description:
Apple no solo actualiza el iPhone cuando aparece una nueva versión de iOS. Existe un sistema menos visible que trabaja en segundo plano y que mucha gente no conoce: las actualizaciones rápidas de seguridad y datos del sistema.
Estas actualizaciones no requieren descargar una versión completa del sistema ni reiniciar el dispositivo. Se aplican de forma automática y están diseñadas para corregir fallos de seguridad urgentes, actualizar bases de datos internas o mejorar el funcionamiento de servicios clave.
Se encuentran dentro de Ajustes, General, Actualización de software, y dependen de una opción llamada “Respuestas de seguridad y archivos del sistema”. Si está activada, el iPhone puede recibir mejoras sin que el usuario tenga que hacer nada.
En este vídeo se explica qué son exactamente estas actualizaciones, qué cambian en el dispositivo, por qué Apple las utiliza cada vez más y qué ventajas tienen frente a las actualizaciones tradicionales de iOS.
videos.fullDescription:
Apple no solo actualiza el iPhone cuando aparece una nueva versión de iOS. Existe un sistema menos visible que trabaja en segundo plano y que mucha gente no conoce: las actualizaciones rápidas de seguridad y datos del sistema.

Estas actualizaciones no requieren descargar una versión completa del sistema ni reiniciar el dispositivo. Se aplican de forma automática y están diseñadas para corregir fallos de seguridad urgentes, actualizar bases de datos internas o mejorar el funcionamiento de servicios clave.

Se encuentran dentro de Ajustes, General, Actualización de software, y dependen de una opción llamada “Respuestas de seguridad y archivos del sistema”. Si está activada, el iPhone puede recibir mejoras sin que el usuario tenga que hacer nada.

En este vídeo se explica qué son exactamente estas actualizaciones, qué cambian en el dispositivo, por qué Apple las utiliza cada vez más y qué ventajas tienen frente a las actualizaciones tradicionales de iOS.

news.title: Cadence Tactile Tablet, la pantalla táctil que permite explorar gráficos, braille y vídeo en tiempo real
news.summary: El acceso a la información digital sigue planteando importantes barreras para las personas ciegas y con discapacidad visual. Aunque las líneas braille y los lectores de pantalla han facilitado considerablemente el uso de ordenadores y dispositivos electrónicos, determinados contenidos, como gráficos, mapas, imágenes o vídeos, continúan siendo difíciles de explorar de forma autónoma. En este […] La entrada Cadence Tactile Tablet, la pantalla táctil que permite explorar gráficos, braille y vídeo en tiempo real se publicó primero en Conticgo .
news.body:
El acceso a la información digital sigue planteando importantes barreras para las personas ciegas y con discapacidad visual. Aunque las líneas braille y los lectores de pantalla han facilitado considerablemente el uso de ordenadores y dispositivos electrónicos, determinados contenidos, como gráficos, mapas, imágenes o vídeos, continúan siendo difíciles de explorar de forma autónoma.

En este contexto surge Cadence Tactile Tablet , un dispositivo desarrollado por la empresa estadounidense Tactile Engineering que propone una nueva forma de interactuar con los contenidos digitales: una pantalla táctil dinámica capaz de representar texto en braille, gráficos e incluso imágenes en movimiento.

A diferencia de las líneas braille tradicionales, que presentan los caracteres de forma secuencial en una única línea, Cadence incorpora una superficie formada por pequeños puntos móviles que pueden elevarse y descender para representar información mediante el tacto.

Su pantalla dispone de 384 puntos táctiles , distribuidos en 48 celdas braille de ocho puntos, organizadas en cuatro líneas de doce celdas. Esta configuración permite consultar varias líneas de texto simultáneamente y explorar representaciones gráficas sin depender exclusivamente de descripciones verbales.

El dispositivo utiliza tecnología MEMS ( Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems ), basada en sistemas microelectromecánicos, para controlar el movimiento de los puntos táctiles. Según el fabricante, estos pueden actualizarse hasta tres veces por segundo, permitiendo modificar la información que aparece bajo los dedos.

Una de las características más llamativas de Cadence es su capacidad para representar gráficos táctiles dinámicos. Esto significa que la superficie no se limita a mostrar una imagen estática, sino que puede modificar los puntos en tiempo real para transmitir información cambiante.

Entre sus posibilidades destacan:

Una demostración especialmente llamativa tuvo lugar durante las 500 Millas de Indianápolis de 2026. Mediante Cadence, los aficionados ciegos pudieron seguir táctilmente el movimiento de los coches en el circuito, convirtiendo la información visual de la carrera en patrones que cambiaban bajo sus dedos.

Esta experiencia muestra cómo la tecnología táctil puede ampliar el acceso no solo a la lectura y al aprendizaje, sino también a acontecimientos deportivos y contenidos audiovisuales.

Otra de sus particularidades es su diseño modular. Cadence puede utilizarse como una unidad independiente o conectarse con otras unidades para ampliar la superficie táctil disponible.

El fabricante contempla configuraciones de hasta cuatro dispositivos conectados, que permiten trabajar con una superficie de mayor tamaño y representar contenidos más amplios.

Además, incorpora teclado braille tipo Perkins, controles direccionales y botones multifunción para navegar por los contenidos, seleccionar líneas, acceder a etiquetas y controlar diferentes aplicaciones.

La conexión con ordenadores y dispositivos compatibles se realiza mediante Bluetooth o USB-C. También dispone de software propio, CadenceOS, que permite gestionar el dispositivo y acceder a diferentes aplicaciones y contenidos.

Las aplicaciones de una pantalla táctil de estas características pueden ser especialmente interesantes en el ámbito educativo.

El acceso a mapas, gráficos matemáticos, representaciones científicas y otros recursos visuales constituye uno de los grandes retos de la educación inclusiva. Aunque existen materiales en relieve y herramientas de adaptación, su elaboración puede requerir tiempo, conocimientos especializados y recursos específicos.

Dispositivos como Cadence permiten explorar nuevas formas de presentar estos contenidos digitalmente, facilitando su actualización y ofreciendo posibilidades de interacción que no proporcionan los materiales táctiles estáticos.

También pueden contribuir al acceso a información que cambia constantemente, como gráficos estadísticos, retransmisiones deportivas o determinadas representaciones audiovisuales.

No obstante, es importante recordar que la disponibilidad de una pantalla táctil dinámica no garantiza por sí sola la accesibilidad de cualquier contenido. La distribución de los puntos, la complejidad de las representaciones y la necesidad de una adaptación comprensible siguen siendo aspectos fundamentales para que la información pueda interpretarse correctamente mediante el tacto.

Cadence Tactile Tablet representa una evolución interesante dentro de la tiflotecnología: pasar de dispositivos centrados principalmente en reproducir texto braille a superficies capaces de transmitir información espacial y dinámica.

Su desarrollo abre nuevas posibilidades para la lectura, la educación, la comunicación y el acceso a contenidos digitales. También plantea una cuestión importante de cara al futuro: cómo conseguir que las imágenes, los gráficos y otros contenidos diseñados originalmente para la vista puedan convertirse en experiencias táctiles realmente comprensibles y accesibles.

La tecnología todavía tiene retos por delante, pero propuestas como esta muestran que el futuro de la accesibilidad digital también pasa por ampliar las posibilidades del sentido del tacto.

Si te ha gustado esta noticia no te pierdas las últimas novedades en tiflotectnología en nuestro apartado de noticias y redes sociales .

Fuente: Tactile Engineering , Double Tap Live .

news.title: Otter AI can now follow conversations across 30+ languages
news.summary: Otter AI just added support for 27 languages and revealed an upcoming feature that can follow along if speakers switch between languages.
news.body:
Otter.ai, the AI-powered note-taking tool, announced Tuesday that it’s expanding its multilingual capabilities, including a new multilingual transcription feature that can follow conversations as speakers switch between languages during the same meeting.

The company is also adding support for 27 languages, its largest language expansion to date. Once the rollout is complete, Otter will support 31 languages in total, making the platform more accessible to international teams.

The upcoming feature will automatically detect language changes and continue transcribing without requiring users to adjust settings. For example, a call could move from English to Korean to Portuguese, with Otter following the conversation throughout.

The update aims to address a common challenge for global teams, where language differences can make meetings and collaboration more difficult.

“Otter is breaking down language barriers so any company, no matter where they’re based, can build a system of record for the decisions for voice AI communication,” an Otter spokesperson told TechCrunch.

Thirteen of the new languages are available now: Mandarin Chinese, Korean, German, Italian, Cantonese, Portuguese, Russian, Indonesian, Malay, Dutch, Turkish, Vietnamese, and Polish.

The remaining 14 languages are coming soon and include Swedish, Danish, Finnish, Arabic, Hindi, Thai, Hebrew, Norwegian, Greek, Macedonian, Persian, Czech, Hungarian, and Romanian.

The newly added languages run on Otter’s own speech models. The company told us it trained them using publicly available datasets and worked with native-speaking volunteers to review transcripts and check accuracy.

The announcement comes as Otter continues to expand beyond transcription and into other workplace AI tools, following its $320 million funding from General Catalyst.

It recently introduced Work Mode, which uses meeting history and connected apps to help users prepare for upcoming calls. For instance, the feature pulls information from previous customer conversations, outstanding action items, notes from teammates’ similar calls, and recent Google Drive files.

Another recent addition is Live Assist, which provides real-time coaching during meetings. It analyzes the conversation and offers relevant suggestions based on what has already been talked about and what is happening in the moment.

news.title: NoteTell Money Reader
news.summary: NoteTell Money Reader is designed to help people who are blind or have low vision identify bills in real time. Simply point the iPhone camera at the bill you want to identify, then hear, feel, or see its value. If you’re blind, have low vision, or are deafblind, NoteTell Money Reader lets you identify bills without any assistance. While shopping, use NoteTell to check your money at the checkout and make sure you get the right change back. You can also use NoteTell to quickly sort your money at home. NoteTell doesn’t require an internet connection, so it identifies bills anywhere, at any time. NoteTell can identify bills at any angle. It is designed to work with bills that are folded, creased, worn, or partly in view. NoteTell is designed to work indoors, outdoors, and even in total darkness. When your environment is too dark to identify bills, NoteTell turns the flashlight on automatically. Vibration Mode tells you the value of each bill as vibrations in your hand—without anyone else hearing it. Each bill has its own vibration pattern. The lowest bill has one pulse, and each higher bill has one more. Pulses come in pairs, so they’re easier to count. Vibration Mode is also useful in noisy places and for people who are deafblind. When VoiceOver is on, double-tap with two fingers to switch between Speech Mode and Vibration Mode. For users with low vision, NoteTell shows the value of each bill in large, high-contrast numbers on the screen. You can complete every task in NoteTell Money Reader using only VoiceOver, without sighted assistance. If you use a braille display with VoiceOver, you can use NoteTell to get the value of each bill in real time. Ask Siri, “Identify currency with NoteTell,” to use NoteTell hands-free. You can also add NoteTell to Control Center or the Lock Screen, assign it to the Action button, or set it up as a Vocal Shortcut. With the full version, you can use Currency Conversion to hear each bill’s value in your home currency when you travel. NoteTell uses on-device processing to identify bills, which means your data never leaves your iPhone. Camera images are never stored on the device or on any servers. You can try the full version free for 14 days. You won’t be charged when the trial ends. You can continue using NoteTell for free to identify the lowest notes of each currency. The full version is also available as a one-time purchase. And with Family Sharing, up to five other people can enjoy your purchase too.

news.title: Why you probably shouldn't buy gadgets with micro USB ports
news.summary: USB-C has largely taken over where micro USB used to reign, but you'll still spot (and should skip using) some devices using the older connector.
news.body:
Micro USB isn't totally extinct, but it's still best avoided if seen.

We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.

USB 1.0 dates back to 1996, and since then, the tech industry has made a mockery of the "universal" part of the acronym by spinning off more variants than Willy Wonka has candy bars. Even on cutting-edge PCs, you'll likely encounter a mix of USB-A and USB-C ports , then spend a few moments trying to figure out where to plug in your USB 4 cables .

Micro USB is one of the most prolific variants, as it helped spread the data and charging benefits of USB to smaller devices. It came after other standards, like mini USB, but it had much more staying power than others. There's a chance you still have a few micro USB products laying around. And despite the wide transition to USB-C, you might even be able to find new cables and accessories to buy today that still use the older connection standard.

When you have a choice, however, it's best to skip micro USB. It's smart to be picky about the charging ports on the products you buy, since micro USB can only hold back their performance and compatibility.

Broadly, the presence of micro USB signifies a product is either old or cutting corners. The format dates back to 2007 — the same year the original iPhone shipped and an eternity in technology. USB-C does presumably raise manufacturing costs, but only relatively. That standard rolled out in 2014, which was well over a decade ago. It's become so common that even cheap USB fans have ditched the micro USB form factor.

More importantly, micro USB is limited to outdated data and power specs. Data speeds are liable to top out at USB 2.0's 480 Mbps, whereas USB 3.0 enables 5 Gbps and USB 4 starts at 40 Gbps. Power might be the true killer, though. Micro USB wall chargers are unlikely to deliver any more than 7.5W, which is practically glacial when some laptops and Android phones use USB-C to top 100W with modern fast charging standards . At the extreme, devices that fully exploit the USB PD (Power Delivery) standard can hit 240W.

The compatibility factor we mentioned impacts convenience. Because micro USB is no longer popular, you'll need to keep different cables around than the ones you use to charge everything else. That takes more space in your bag when packing and occupies outlet slots that could be used for additional USB-C cables. Adapters can help, but they're clunky. There's also the practical matter of micro USB not being reversible like USB-C, so you'll have to fumble around to find the right orientation every so often. It's far easier to accidentally bend the pins in the older standard.

As time goes on, it will be increasingly hard to find any new micro USB products, similarly to how you can't waltz into a local big-box retailer and assume there will be composite cables for an old VCR. You're certainly not going to find micro USB ports on any new smartphone or computer.

For some gadget categories, there's nothing inherently wrong with micro USB. Wireless earbuds, for example, don't have terribly large batteries to fill, so even 7.5W may be enough to charge them quickly. I used to own Apple's micro USB-based Powerbeats3 buds, and you could get an hour of listening from them with five minutes of charging. As for data, 480Mbps should be plenty fast for file transfers under a gigabyte.

In most cases, it's worth holding onto the micro USB devices you already have. There's no sense spending money or generating e-waste if the port is the only drawback of a device. Just keep a dedicated charging cable handy for your older Kindle, flashlight, game controller or similar. But when it comes to buying new, look for USB-C. You'll likely get superior performance, and might actually save cash in the long run if it means not having to buy another product prematurely when micro USB's weaknesses rear their head.

USB-C has advantages even within the categories where micro USB can have value. For instance, while the Powerbeats3 offered up to 12 hours without a case, the Powerbeats Pro 2 come with a USB-C charging case that enables up to 45 hours of total playback. It's hard to imagine that case being feasible at all with micro USB.

news.title: Everything we know so far about the Nvidia spy scandal targeting CEO Jensen Huang
news.summary: The leather-jacketed CEO of Nvidia, Jensen Huang, has acknowledged an affair with Megaspeed exec Alice Huang, spurring an investigation by his company and intense discussions worldwide. Recent reporting noted that since last year, US intelligence reports had identified Alice Huang (no relation) as not only the exec for an AI compute company renting access to […]
news.body:
The leather-jacketed CEO of Nvidia, Jensen Huang, has acknowledged an affair with Megaspeed exec Alice Huang, spurring an investigation by his company and intense discussions worldwide. Recent reporting noted that since last year, US intelligence reports had identified Alice Huang (no relation) as not only the exec for an AI compute company renting access to Nvidia GPUs, but also a spy for China’s Ministry of State Security.

In recent years, Nvidia has become a key part of the Trump administration’s AI push, a central figure in negotiations over potential Chinese access to cutting-edge AI hardware, and a company that has used its now $4 trillion-plus market cap to finance other AI companies, including the “neoclouds” like Coreweave who have been some of its biggest customers. So far, Nvidia and Jensen Huang have said that they have “no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised,” but that hasn’t settled things as the investigation continues.

news.title: Hotel giant Wyndham exposed customer data after app security lapse
news.summary: Exclusive: Wyndham left a hardcoded credential in its customer app, allowing anyone to access customer data. The hotel giant wouldn't say if it has the ability to check for any past unauthorized access.
news.body:
Hotel and resort giant Wyndham has acknowledged a cybersecurity incident after a good-faith security researcher discovered a bug that allowed anyone to access customers’ personal information.

Security researcher Robert Wiggins at What Security exclusively told TechCrunch that he found a password inside the source code of Wyndham’s Android app, which granted access to an internal company database, hosted by tech company Salesforce.

Wiggins told TechCrunch that the credential exposed personal information including customer names, email addresses, and Wyndham member numbers. The database also stores customer login tokens ( called JWTs ) that keep customers logged-in to their apps without having to repeatedly enter their own passwords. The database also contained Wyndham files and documents.

According to Wiggins, the database had millions of entries, but he was unable to determine an accurate number of exposed customer records. Wyndham touts some 129 million enrolled rewards members.

The researcher said Wyndham has no way to report security flaws, and asked for TechCrunch’s help in alerting the company. Soon after TechCrunch made contact with Wyndham’s cybersecurity staff, the exposed credential was revoked, preventing any further access to the database.

“Our team has taken steps to address the issue,” a Wyndham spokesperson told TechCrunch. “Our security teams have no evidence of any unauthorized access,” the statement added, without providing any further details about the claim.

Wyndham’s spokesperson would not say, when asked, whether the company had the technical means, such as server logs, to determine if anyone had access to the customer database prior to Wiggins’ discovery.

TechCrunch also asked Wyndham whether it planned to notify customers whose information was exposed, or disclose the incident to U.S. regulators, such as filing a notice with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, as public companies are required to do for material cybersecurity incidents. Wyndham would not say.

Wyndham’s spokesperson also would not say for how long the password was embedded in its customer app, or how Wyndham plans to ship a long-term fix for the app.

App and software developers generally avoid including passwords or credentials in publicly released software and apps — a process known as “hardcoding” — as anyone with a copy of the software can extract the password and use it to access its associated server or database. Given the simplicity with which credentials can be abused by anyone, many cases of hardcoded credentials are automatically scored with a maximum vulnerability severity rating.

For Wiggins, this is his second public discovery of hardcoded credentials in two weeks, after finding a near-identical vulnerability in Applebee’s app that exposed customer data. Wiggins relied on AI tools for both discoveries, which make it easier to identify simple security weaknesses, such as hardcoded credentials, by scouring thousands of lines of decompiled app code every second.

When asked about Wyndham’s response, Wiggins told TechCrunch that he was glad the company fixed the issue, but noted that without visibility into any past activity, someone with malicious intent could have leaked large amounts of customers’ personal information.

The company would not say whether it planned to set up a vulnerability disclosure program to allow outside security researchers and hackers to privately report security vulnerabilities.

Michael Francess, Wyndham’s cybersecurity director who responded to the incident, told TechCrunch that researchers can alert [email protected] with details of potential security issues. The company’s spokesperson would not say whether it plans to change its website to allow researchers to alert the company.

This is the latest known security incident at Wyndham in recent years. In 2024, a security researcher found several Wyndham hotel check-in desks were running remote-access spyware that was leaking screenshots of guest records and booking information to the open web.

Soon after our reporting, the spyware app found on the hotel computers, called pcTattletale, was hacked and its banks of customer data stolen, forcing the company’s owner, Bryan Fleming, to shut down the company. Fleming, a former resident of Michigan, was later arrested by federal authorities and convicted of making, selling, and advertising unlawful spyware.

news.title: The pros and cons of using mesh Wi-Fi
news.summary: Should you buy a mesh Wi-Fi system or a standalone router? Learn how each handles range, roaming, and cost, and which one fits your home best.
news.body:
Mesh covers more ground, but a standalone router may be all you need.

We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.

Diving into Wi-Fi routers for the first time can be baffling. There are a lot of concepts to understand, and not just the differences between Wi-Fi 6 and 7 . Speeds and features vary between models using the same specification, and it may not be clear which of your devices can (or should) connect to which frequency bands.

One of the biggest purchasing decisions is whether to go with a mesh Wi-Fi system or stick to a standalone router. Most people probably default to standalone products, since they're cheaper. In fact, given the price gap, it's important to have concrete reasons for stepping up to a mesh product.

The value of mesh systems mostly boils down to range and seamless roaming. In some situations, however, a standalone router may not only be acceptable, but preferable. Here's how to decide which option is right for you.

The main advantage of mesh Wi-Fi is range. In a mesh system, each satellite router acts as a sort of repeater for the gateway router that connects to your modem or fiber terminal. In theory, a relatively cheap kit like an Eero 7 two-pack can cover up to 4,000 square feet. If you need more coverage, you just add another compatible router. Conversely, standalone products have a fixed coverage radius unless you buy a Wi-Fi extender .

Unlike extenders, mesh systems enable seamless transitions. There are no separate SSIDs (network IDs) — they simply hand devices off from one unit to another based on how close they are. This avoids the hassle of manual SSID selection and the problems that sometimes arise when devices need to talk to each other and assume a shared network. You also get more consistent speeds, as a signal should never degrade much unless you roam into the wider world.

This seamlessness comes with downsides beyond price. Since mesh products depend on unified SSIDs, you can't assign separate IDs for each frequency band; band steering is automatic. I know from experience that mesh routers can trip up cheap 2.4GHz-only smart home accessories because their setup apps often can't find them when your phone is on 5 or 6GHz. On the flip side, you might want to force devices like PCs or VR headsets over to 5 or 6GHz for the best possible bandwidth.

It's also worth noting that with cheaper mesh products, the backhaul between routers sometimes shares the same bands as connecting devices. When that happens, performance can suffer considerably. If you don't have the budget for a tri- or quad-band system, there may not be much point in going with mesh technology unless filling in dead zones is all that matters.

Mesh is the obvious choice if you live in a multi-floor house, or want coverage in your backyard, detached shed or garage. A standalone router can cause smart home conflicts and create slow or dead zones, especially since metal and concrete can block signals. When interference persists, some mesh systems will even let you set up a wired Ethernet backhaul as a workaround.

Most apartments should be thoroughly covered by a standalone router unless you're encountering specific speed or range issues. You're better off saving your money or putting the savings toward a faster router.

There are some borderline cases. For instance, some multi-floor homes are small enough to be covered by a single router. If you want to push the limits, place your router in a relatively central location, and keep it unobscured by anything that might harm signal quality. Think of your router as a radio station — you wouldn't expect to hear the news clearly if the broadcast tower were on the opposite side of a mountain.

news.title: Apple Intelligence completes regulatory registration for iPad and Mac in China
news.summary: Apple has completed an important regulatory step ahead of Apple Intelligence’s expected launch in China this December. Here are the details. more…
news.body:
Apple has completed an important regulatory step ahead of Apple Intelligence’s expected launch in China this December. Here are the details.

In late October, Apple published a press release on its Chinese Newsroom website confirming its intention to launch Apple Intelligence in China this December, as part of iOS 27.3.

Apple went on to release the first iOS 27.3 developer beta a few days later, allowing users in China to test Apple Intelligence ahead of its public launch.

In its press release, however, Apple also noted that the initial rollout would be limited to iPhones, as support for other platforms was still pending regulatory approval.

Now, as spotted by Reuters , Apple Intelligence “has been ‌registered for use on tablets and laptops in China, Shanghai’s cyberspace regulator said on Monday.”

For context, generative AI services must complete a regulatory registration process before they can launch publicly in China.

Apple Intelligence, which, in China, relies on Alibaba’s Qwen model to power certain AI features, had already received regulatory approval for iPhones in July, following months of delays and negotiations with Chinese authorities.

With today’s registration, Apple has cleared another regulatory hurdle ahead of Apple Intelligence’s launch in China. However, the company has yet to confirm whether iPad and Mac support will also arrive in December.

To read Reuters ‘ full report, follow this link .

news.title: Today’s macOS updates fix security gap involving eMudhra certificates
news.summary: Apple today released macOS updates that address a security gap involving compromised eMudhra certificates, after initially blocking them in Safari, Mail, and other apps in October. Here are the details. more…
news.body:
Apple today released macOS updates that address a security gap involving compromised eMudhra certificates, after initially blocking them in Safari, Mail, and other apps in October. Here are the details.

A few weeks ago, Mozilla reported that private keys of eight intermediate certificate authorities operated by eMudhra, an Indian digital certification company, had been compromised.

In essence, these certificates are used to establish trust in digital certificates that verify website identities and enable secure connections.

With access to the compromised private keys, bad actors could potentially create fraudulent certificates that appear legitimate, allowing them to impersonate websites and intercept sensitive user information.

In response to the compromise, Apple began automatically blocking the affected certificates on October 19, followed by additional protections on October 23.

These changes were delivered through automatic certificate configuration updates, meaning users didn’t need to install a macOS update to be protected.

While these measures protected Safari, Mail, and apps that use Apple’s networking and security frameworks, they didn’t cover all of macOS, as certain command-line tools, including curl and git, could still accept the compromised certificates.

At the time, Apple published a support article with instructions for administrators to manually address this remaining security gap, while promising a fix in a future macOS update.

Today, Apple updated the document to confirm that the fix is now available.

As Apple explains, macOS 27.2.1, macOS 26.7.3, and macOS 15.8.3, released earlier today , prevent the affected command-line tools from accepting the compromised certificates, eliminating the need for administrators to manually address the issue.

The updates also remove five root CA certificates from /etc/ssl/cert.pem, including three additional eMudhra certificates that weren’t part of Apple’s original manual workaround.

Still, for users who are unable to install the latest macOS updates, Apple continues to provide instructions for manually addressing the issue in its support document, along with the names and SHA-256 fingerprints of the 12 affected certificates and five root CA certificates removed by the updates.

Apple also notes that “some apps and tools include their own list of root CA certificates and don’t use Apple’s block or /etc/ssl/cert.pem,” and advises users to contact the developer of those apps and tools.

To read Apple’s full support document, follow this link .

news.title: Apple starts offering $50 extended usage packs for AI features in Creator Studio
news.summary: It'll cost you to access Logic Pro's AI assistant after you reach the monthly usage limit.
news.body:
It’ll cost you to access Logic Pro’s AI assistant after you reach the monthly usage limit.

Apple has made it clear for a while that Siri AI is bound by daily usage limits and that it will offer expanded access via iCloud+ plans. The company hasn't shed more light on exactly how that will work, but it has revealed how Creator Studio users can continue wielding the AI features of those apps after they reach the regular limits.

It has started selling $50 intelligence usage packs for Creator Studio, and Logic Pro is the first app to support these. Apple updated Logic Pro last month to include an assistant that's powered by its own models as well as those from third parties. The company said the chatbot can help "creators and producers navigate production workflows, start a new song, set up a vocal track from a single prompt or refine an active project."

As noted by 9to5Mac , folks can view their AI usage in the app by going to Logic Pro on the menu bar, then Intelligence Features > Show Usage . The window that pops up includes a Buy More Usage button — clicking this takes you to the option to buy an intelligence usage pack.

A support page explains that users with active Apple Creator Studio subscriptions in the US, UK, Canada, Brazil, France, Germany, India and Mexico can buy intelligence usage packs to keep using AI features after they reach their monthly usage limit. A pack is tied to the Apple Account used to purchase it — there's no Family Sharing support.

"Unused additional usage purchased with intelligence usage packs roll over from month to month and expire 12 months after purchase," Apple added. "Additional usage gets consumed for relevant features only after you've reached your monthly limit in any given month."

It seems likely that Apple will expand intelligence usage packs to other Creator Studio apps, such as Final Cut Pro and Pixelmator Pro. It's interesting that Apple is opting for this approach over a regular subscription, but perhaps the company has other offerings planned for the future. For what it's worth, Creator Studio apps are available via a subscription or one-time purchase .

news.title: A Sam Altman parody offers an amusing lesson in memory management
news.summary: We verified the RAM numbers are real without sending any emails to OpenAI.
news.body:
Sam Altman's recent comments on the Cheeky Pint podcast inspired developer Iain Kay to create a satirical script that allows users to email the OpenAI CEO once per day if more than 10 percent of their system RAM is reported as available. Ram-Altman is described by its creator as a "parody project" launched in response to Altman's viral remarks about RAM in your personal PC.

As reported by The Verge , on the October 29 episode recorded with Stripe President John Collison, Altman said, "A lot of people want local inference. And somehow, they assume that the problem is solved now because we are going to have open source models, we’re going to be able to run them on our computers, and so we’re not going to need all the stuff in the data center. But from a global allocation perspective, actually, it’s quite terrible to have everybody have a bunch of the world’s limited supply of DRAM sitting in their own computer and being used 5 percent of the time."

Altman has since explained that his comments were taken out of context and briefly changed his display name to "RAM Altman" on X, which Kay calls on the project GitHub, "objectively excellent and where the project gets its name."

news.title: Vulnerability that lets hackers SSH into Linux devices is under active exploitation
news.summary: "*sshole" poses a serious threat to Internet security.
news.body:
Hackers are actively exploiting a recently discovered critical vulnerability that allows them to log in to privileged accounts on many Linux systems, multiple researchers are reporting.

The vulnerability, tracked under the name *sshole, arises from the interaction between OpenSSH and a code library known as musl. Linux systems that use both of these packages and meet certain other requirements can be hacked to give unauthenticated access to high-privilege accounts in a matter of seconds. *sshole became publicly known last Thursday and quickly stoked concerns it could lead to widespread compromise of Linux machines. Four days later, the prediction shows signs of becoming real.

Security firm Greynoise said Monday that honeypots it maintains in Southeast Asia have come under attack by a group it’s tracking as GT10. The group conducted “mature intrusions" into the systems, which Greynoise uses to detect attempted or successful attacks in real time. Greynoise subsequently gained access to a GT10 server that revealed potential other victims and some of the tools used in the campaign. A backdoor the group is using in the attacks contains Chinese language comments and appears to be generated with the use of AI.

news.title: Apple Releases Version 27.2.1 of iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and watchOS with Bug Fixes and Security Updates
news.summary: Apple has today released version 27.2.1 of iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and watchOS, bringing bug fixes and security updates, including for a vulnerability that allowed macOS command line tools to use compromised eMudhra certificates. As the 27.2.1 updates were not distributed to external testers prior to their release, we do not have any information on whether they contain any accessibility fixes for blind, deaf blind, or low vision users at the time of writing. However, as these updates appear to have been released to address a small number of specific issues, we do not expect them to contain any such fixes. news.title: Jensen Huang’s affair with alleged Chinese spy puts Nvidia’s China ambitions under scrutiny
news.summary: Jensen Huang’s alleged affair with a suspected Chinese spy threatens to complicate Nvidia’s lobbying efforts to loosen U.S. chip export restrictions and maintain access to China’s lucrative AI market.
news.body:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has never been quiet about his belief that the U.S. should continue selling AI chips to China, rather than shutting the country off from the technology. The revelation that he had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy threatens to complicate that argument.

The Financial Times reported Friday on Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive at Megaspeed, an Nvidia customer. Jensen Huang admitted to the affair and apologized in a memo to the company on Sunday. U.S. intelligence officials believe Alice Huang was recruited by Chinese intelligence to gather information about the CEO and influence the company’s efforts to loosen chip export restrictions.

Nvidia’s independent directors, working with outside legal counsel, are investigating the matter, and Congress is already demanding answers .

The controversy comes at a sensitive moment for Nvidia. Historically, China has been a big market for the company. It has shrunk in recent years due to strict U.S. export controls and an aggressive push by Beijing for domestic alternatives. In the three months ended July 26, Nvidia recorded $7.9 billion in revenue from customers headquartered in China, roughly 8% of total revenue.

Huang has repeatedly lobbied the U.S. government to expand access to China , and some of his persuasion tactics have been successful. Huang met repeatedly with President Donald Trump and administration officials last year; afterward, the government reversed restrictions on Nvidia’s H20 chips and allowed exports of its more powerful H200 processors.

On numerous occasions, Huang has publicly lamented export controls, calling them a “ failure ” at a conference last year and saying in May that it was “ not wise ” for the U.S. and China to create two distinct AI ecosystems. He has also warned that shutting Nvidia out of China’s compute market would enable the country to develop its own AI chips to challenge Nvidia internationally.

China is already moving in that direction. Reuters reported last week that about 600,000 H200 chips are being held in Hong Kong, awaiting shipment to mainland China. Beijing is pushing AI companies to prioritize buying chips from Chinese companies instead.

The idea that Huang needed any encouragement in the form of an attractive woman to push for greater access to China seems like a stretch, particularly because his lobbying efforts predate their reported meeting at an Nvidia event in early 2024. At the end of the day, Huang is a salesman trying to dominate one of the world’s biggest AI markets.

Still, the allegations involving Alice Huang open new scrutiny of the company’s business relationships and could taint any assurances Nvidia offers that it can prevent sensitive technology from reaching unauthorized customers.

Once made, rumors of questionable allegiances can be hard to shake. Secretary of State Marco Rubio reportedly warned officials close to Trump earlier this year about Huang’s relationship with an alleged spy. Even if Nvidia’s investigation finds that Huang didn’t share secrets with his paramour, the question is whether he’ll be able to convince Washington that Nvidia can still responsibly do business with China.

Nvidia did not respond to a request for comment.

news.title: Claude Code is accidentally exposing secrets all over GitHub
news.summary: "Do not ask again" prompt leads to passwords, API keys, and more being shared.
news.body:
Claude Code is leaking sensitive information on public GitHub instances thanks to a partial oversight in the way its settings files are handled. That's the finding of AI security researchers at Apiiro, who discovered thousands of secrets , including database passwords, API tokens, and root logins, amid Claude Code settings files embedded in GitHub repositories.

The leak stems from the way Claude Code handles user approval for automated shell commands. When a user chooses the "Yes, and don't ask again" option to approve running a command, that choice gets stored as part of a rule in the local ".claude/settings.local.json" file on the user's computer. That rule is sometimes coded as a pattern, but the command itself is often written to that settings file as is, including any sensitive information that may be embedded within it.

This isn't really a significant security issue if the settings file stays on the user's local machine (assuming that machine doesn't become compromised itself, of course). And Anthropic notes in its Claude Code documentation that this particular settings file gets added to the developer's global .gitignore list , which usually prevents it from being shared publicly.

news.summary: Hola gente, ¿qué tal les va?
news.body:
Hola gente, ¿qué tal les va?

Después de bastante tiempo trabajando en un proyecto nuevo y distinto dentro de la familia TCA Software, ¡por fin llega TCA DjMix 1.0!

Si eres de los que creció viendo a algún DJ mezclar pistas con fundidos suaves y sincronizando beats al milisegundo… pues este es tu programa. Y lo mejor: está diseñado desde cero para que cualquiera pueda usarlo con lector de pantalla.

Sí, lo has leído bien. TCA DjMix es la primera aplicación de DJ accesible para Windows pensada específicamente para quienes usamos NVDA, JAWS o Narrador. Pero no es solo para nosotros: cualquier persona puede usarla con teclado, con ratón o incluso con una controladora MIDI.

Y esto tiene algo todavía más especial: este es el primer programa de toda la familia TCA Software que fue construido usando Inteligencia Artificial. Sí, justo como lo lees. Por primera vez en la historia de TCA Software, creamos un programa "by coding" con ayuda de IA.

TCA DjMix es una aplicación de mezcla musical accesible que reúne todo lo necesario para crear tus sesiones. Estas son sus funciones clave:

• Biblioteca unificada y platos independientes

TCA DjMix incluye una biblioteca centralizada donde cargas tu carpeta de música, la cual se navega 100% con lector de pantalla y lista todos los archivos automáticamente (formatos compatibles: WAV, FLAC, OGG, MP3 y AIFF). Desde esa misma lista puedes cargar las pistas de manera independiente en el plato 1 o en el plato 2 usando los atajos (Alt+1 o Alt+2), controlando el volumen y la reproducción de cada plato por separado.

• Sincronización automática de BPM (Beatmatch)

• F5 / F6: Reproducir o pausar el plato 1 / plato 2.

• F7 / F8: Detener el plato 1 / plato 2.

• Tab: Recorrer controles.

• Ctrl+B: Sincronizar el plato activo con el otro plato.

• Ctrl+S: Detener todos los samples.

• Ctrl+P: Abrir la configuración.

• Ctrl+J: Panel de controladora MIDI.

news.body:
Tras una candidata a liberación, NV Access ha anunciado mediante esta publicación que ya se encuentra disponible para su descarga la versión final de NVDA 2026.3.1, el lector de pantalla gratuito y de código abierto para Microsoft Windows. Se recomienda a todos los usuarios actualizar a esta nueva versión, cuyo uso se considera apto también en entornos de producción.

Esta versión contiene un parche que resuelve incidencias de seguridad. También corrige un fallo introducido en NVDA 2026.3 con el conmutador de tareas de Windows 10. Se ha restaurado la voz de Espeak NG en portugués de Brasil al comportamiento que tenía en NVDA 2026.2. Tan pronto como actualices NVDA, no olvides reiniciar el equipo. El reinicio garantiza que se pueden actualizar archivos que antes no se podían modificar porque estaban abiertos para escritura. En la práctica, al reiniciar vuelven a funcionar aplicaciones basadas en Electron, tales como Teams, Dropbox o Google Drive, y dejan de producirse comportamientos extraños con el explorador de archivos, Thunderbird, Office y algunos navegadores. Reiniciar es lo primero que debes hacer antes de informar de cualquier fallo. Hazlo pulsando windows+d para ir al escritorio, alt+f4, e intro sobre la opción Reiniciar. Puedes descargar NVDA 2026.3, así como las últimas versiones compatibles con sistemas antiguos y material útil para desarrolladores, desde nuestra página de descargas . La suma SHA256 de NVDA 2026.3.1, que se usa para garantizar la integridad de la descarga, es 6f80a5b0ca720a7d0d314b5be212f37388bbe81a1107ac3298c1821a1cd3f052. Si tienes una versión estable anterior, también puedes actualizar automáticamente desde el menú Ayuda. Y desde la rc1, con el complemento Selector del canal de actualización, se puede hacer del mismo modo configurando previamente el canal estable. Si todavía no conoces NVDA y quieres leer algo más sobre él antes de probarlo, te recomendamos consultar la guía de usuario y la referencia rápida de órdenes . Si te gustan nuestros proyectos y el contenido que ofrecemos, plantéate contribuir mensualmente con una pequeña cantidad. Tan sólo un euro es capaz de marcar la diferencia y ayudarnos a mejorar. Visita la página de donaciones para obtener más información, o la tienda para hacerte con libros de formación traducidos y sintetizadores de voz de alta calidad. ¡Feliz lunes!

news.title: How To Route Screen Reader Audio To Different Devices With Sandfly Screen Reader
news.summary: There is no need to explain why a screen reader user might sometimes want to have the screen reader’s audio routed to a different audio…
news.body:
Published 8 November 2026 by Kareen Kiwan

There is no need to explain why a screen reader user might sometimes want to have the screen reader’s audio routed to a different audio device than the default one.

On Android, this is not natively possible. Samsung’s One UI offers a workaround through the Separate App Sound feature, which gets the job done, even if it is not perfect. However, to my knowledge, other OEMs do not offer a comparable feature.

TalkBack, Android’s default built-in screen reader, does not offer a similar capability either. Sandfly , an open-source screen reader, allows users to change the device used to output the screen reader’s speech and audio. It also provides an option to route the audio to the phone’s speaker when specific audio devices are connected.

Sandfly is not the only screen reader that provides this feature. Another screen reader that offers similar functionality is Backtalk , and other screen readers might have something similar. However, this post only covers how to use the audio output feature found in Sandfly. Note that setting up Sandfly is outside the scope of this post.

Open Sandfly settings. You can access them from the Sandfly menu or by selecting Sandfly from the list of installed accessibility services. You can also access the settings by selecting the app from the apps list.

Find “Audio output” and activate it.

Then, press “Audio output device” to see a list of currently available audio devices, including System Default, Phone Speaker, and connected wired and wireless audio devices.

Select any device to route Sandfly’s audio through it.

To have the audio come out of the phone’s speaker when a certain device is connected, choose “Phone speaker with these devices” and check all the devices you want. Whenever one of the selected devices is connected, Sandfly’s audio will come out of the phone’s speaker instead of the connected device.

Use the “Keep speech on the phone while casting” option to determine whether you want the screen reader’s audio to come out of the phone’s speaker when you cast your screen.

Although Sandfly is not my primary screen reader at the moment, I tested Audio Output and was impressed by the reliability of the audio routing. I was able to switch between Bluetooth headphones, wired USB-C earbuds, and the phone’s speakers without any issues or interference with media playback. This is consistent with tests conducted by other team members, including full-time Sandfly users.

Published in Tips and Tricks Tutorials

news.title: Evermyth - God Life Simulator
news.summary: Become a god. Rule the world. Evermyth is a mythic life sim where you play a god from your very first prayer. Choose your domain, win the faithful, build an island realm, fall in love and face the other gods. Every life is a new myth, and every choice is yours. CHOOSE 1 OF 12 DOMAINS Death, War, Love, Sea, Sky, Nature, Knowledge, Order, Chaos, Craft, Fortune or Hearth. Each plays differently, with its own powers, prayers and stories. Be born to your seat, spring from the world itself, rise from mortal life, or seize the throne from the god before you. CREATE YOUR GOD Shape your face, hair, eyes, crown and robes in hand-drawn art inspired by ancient Greek pottery. Name your cult, choose its sacred sign, and fill a pantheon of twelve with Greek, Roman or Egyptian gods, or invent your own. WIELD 400+ DIVINE POWERS Send the rain. Hurl thunder at the assembly. Curse a king. Raise the dead. Awaken five aspects of your domain and unleash great acts: drown the world in a flood, raise a golden city, or walk among mortals in disguise. ANSWER PRAYERS, SHAPE MORTAL LIVES 400+ prayers, nearly 700 events and 240+ story chains that unfold across years. Shipwrecks, secrets, plagues, weddings, prophecies and family feuds. Every choice has a price, and mortals remember what you did. FACE CALAMITY Locust years, plague ships, great fires, a waking mountain. Save your people, bargain with another god, or let the world burn. WAGE WAR Rival realms want your island. Read your scouts and fight round by round: charge, hold the line, flank, or call down your domain to turn the battle. Sack cities, take tribute or make peace. RAISE A DIVINE BEAST Dragon, kraken, leviathan, hydra, basilisk, great wolf, golden lion, shadow panther, nine-tailed fox, star stag or moon moth. Feed it, train it, fly together, and loose it on your enemies before a hero comes hunting. LOVE, SCHEME AND FEUD Flirt, feast, beguile, trade favors and hold grudges. Marry, raise godborn children, and decide which of them deserves your seat. Win the favor of every court, from the God of the Sky to the smallest river nymph. GODS CAN FALL Rivals and even your own children can challenge you to a contest to the death. Win, and end them the old ways: cast into the pit, chained beneath a mountain, torn apart or swallowed whole. Lose, and your myth may end there. BUILD YOUR REALM Raise temples, markets, harbors, theaters and a Colossus. Keep nobles, priests and commoners on your side, or rule by fear. Change your island's climate, dress your city in your colors, and watch it come alive from dawn to night. GROW YOUR FAITH Turn a handful of believers into ten thousand faithful. Found oracles, ordain a high priest and choose the doctrines of your worship. LIVE A GOD'S OWN LIFE Wander the world as yourself, a mortal or a beast. Visit the Oracle and the Fates, take up pastimes, witness rare wonders, and earn epithets like the Merciful, Godslayer or Ender of Ages. BECOME A LEGEND Pass your seat to an heir and play on as them, or rise to the sky and set yourself among the stars. Every ended myth joins your Hall of Myths. Then begin again as a new god in a new age. PLAY YOUR WAY Free to play with no time limit. Three difficulties, from Gentle to Cruel. Day, evening and night modes. Plays offline, and no accounts, ads, subscriptions, energy timers or currencies.

news.title: Corner Grocer: Market Sim
news.summary: Run a little neighborhood market. Order stock, fill the shelves, set your prices, ring up customers at the register, and grow your shop from a corner store into a premium market with a second branch. Corner Grocer is a market management game built to be played with VoiceOver from the very first day. Sighted players and VoiceOver players play the same game with the same rules. A DAY AT THE MARKET • Morning: check deliveries, prices and today's event, then place your orders in the office. • Open: customers come in, ask for help and queue up. Scan their items, take cash or card, and count out the change. • Stock: open crates in the stockroom, put goods on the right shelves and watch the dates. Goods go off, and a wrong shelf sells less. • Evening: read the report, get one clear tip for tomorrow and decide what to invest in. GROW • Start with an empty corner shop and a basket of bread. Earn, then invest: shelves, fridges, freezers, produce stands, bakery cases and deli counters in build mode. • Move up through four store sizes: corner shop, mini market, big market and premium market. • License new product lines. There are 48 products, from bread and milk to hummus, pet food and olive oil. • Open extra registers and hire cashiers. Your own register is always yours. • Much later, open a second branch run by a manager you choose, and read its result in the evening report. • Invest in upgrades, supplier contracts and campaigns. Contracts and campaigns can renew themselves. • In the office, one button fills your order from the suggestions. In the stockroom, one button places every crate that has room. • Daily goals, 22 achievements, and events such as heat waves, rain, power cuts, rival sales and supplier delays. • There is no final day. Play as long as you like. BUILT FOR VOICEOVER • Every station has labelled controls in a fixed order, plus actions for the rotor. Anything you can drag also has a way to do without dragging. • Three speech levels: Full, Balanced and Sounds First. • Magic Tap pauses and resumes the day. • Sound carries information: door chimes, scanner beeps, queue alerts, shelf warnings. The Listening Room in Settings plays every sound and tells you what it means. • Easy, Normal and Custom modes, with assists for patience, day length, customer flow, wrong-shelf protection, undo and clearing spoiled goods each morning. Assists are for everyone and always free. • Short optional small jobs fill the quiet moments at the register. • Customer voices are generated with AI. You can turn them down or off in Settings. MAKE IT YOURS Decorate your shop in the Shop Studio: floors, walls, counters, signs, lights, decor and outfits, plus atmospheres, music albums and end-of-day tunes. Name your shop and let the game describe it to you. FREE TO PLAY, WITH OPTIONAL ADS AND PURCHASES The game is free to download. Cash from the shop pays for stock, shelves and upgrades. Coins are only for sound and looks, and never make the game easier or harder. You can earn Coins by playing and by watching optional ads, or buy Coin packs. Coin packs and support packs are optional in-app purchases. Accessibility features and Easy mode are always free. ADS Ads come from Google AdMob. Optional ads in the evening report and the Shop Studio give 10 Coins each, up to 3 a day. Without VoiceOver, a short full-screen ad can also play between days from day 5. Players using VoiceOver never get forced ads. Any support pack (Starter, Supporter or Founder) removes ads. Ads are personalised only if you allow tracking when the game asks. Play in 11 languages: English, Turkish, German, Spanish, French, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese (Brazil), Russian and Chinese (Simplified). Customers speak all 11 languages. English and Turkish voices come with the app; the others download once while you are online. Questions or feedback: support@birkinapps.com

news.title: The Day Bingo Went to Brent Cross, Met the iPhone Duo, and Bought a Pizza
news.summary: Introduction Dear old Brent Cross has featured quite heavily in my life. When I was a child, it was a brand spanking new shopping centre, famed for being absolutely enormous as well as the first attempt outside London to bring shopping and entertainment together. London had its west end, and we in north London had our north-west end in Brent Cross. My family, certain of whom have a worrying fixation with shopping trips, used to love it. Later in life, Brent Cross was where I went to get my wedding suit made. Note, dear gentleman readers, that I had my suit made, not hired, and and you should not allow yourselves to be wed in someone else's clothes either. After all, is the bride going to hire her wedding dress? Brent Cross is also where our Apple Store is, and last Saturday I persuaded Mrs Bingo to come along with me and meet the new iPhone line-up. Now, notwithstanding I've been to Brent Cross many times, I've never been on a Saturday afternoon. Don't! It's phenomenally busy and immediately put pay to the idea that I might capture a nice, atmospheric audio review of my iPhone explorations. Audio there is, but it is unfit for human consumption. Plus, although we've both been to the Apple Store there a couple of times, we had forgotten where it was. Cue a quarter of an hour wandering around past every chain store imaginable alongside coffee shops and a pop-up pizzeria, which admittedly we noted down as a place to visit on the way out, we finally remembered it was on the upper level and got there in in the end. It was the work of a moment to find a demo iPhone Duo model with which to play, safely cabled to the counter as a countermeasure to light-fingered iProdders. Let the games begin, as they say. What This Review is, and What it Ain't I want to kick off by setting some parameters. These are my unfiltered impressions. I'm not a tech journalist so I'll not be getting down and dirty with the processing power or what have you. I'm also assuming you're someone who either has the budget for the duo or who is at least very curious and perhaps wishes they had. So I'll be entirely subjective about whether it's worth the money—ultimately, that's a value judgement for each and every one of us. There may be a bit of repetition if you're familiar with other iPhone Duo pioneers' output, like the excellent Dave Nason's contributions, and if that happens it's purely coincidental, and a byproduct of my giving you my unfiltered impressions. But I have tried to keep this to a minimum and I also cross-refer to Dave's contribution, so please look at that if you haven't already. For you braillists out there, you'll be pleased to learn I did get a good go at BSI. Still reading? Thank gawd for that! A Jet-Setter's Passport Those who say the Duo is like a passport are not wrong. It really is more or less the same size and shape. I'm not talking a passport that most people have, however. I mean a passport like my mate Penguin has, because he is sent to so many foreign parts by his employer. In the UK, we have a choice of adding a good few extra pages to our passport if we're like Penguin. the Duo's like Penguin's passport, so a bit thicker than mine. Never mind Penguin, Bingo! How does it feel in the hand? Honestly? Fantastic. Size, weight, everything. I can't fault it. True, I couldn't test it in the pocket as I suspect various alarms would have gone off and I did not have a pocket at quite the right height what with its being cabled to the table and all that lark, but I could tell there'd be no trouble fitting it in any but the smallest of pockets. Dave Nason has commented on the weight. I have to say, I didn't find this at all noticeable. It is, perhaps, the weight of a wallet with a reasonable number of coins in it. That's what it feels like to hold. Not a wallet stuffed full to the seams, but a wallet with a handful of change in it. I say that on the assumption that anyone can still remember what carrying cash was like. Now, I admit I didn't hold it in my hand for very long, whereas Dave has actually been using one; but even allowing for that I was not at all concerned. Sure, it's heavier than an iPhone Air, but that's what you expect. Know When to Fold Up Dave has covered this in some detail already. For my part, I found the magnetic snap as the Duo folded very satisfying. The thing looks a very robust piece of kit when folded. When unfolded, in small tablet mode, it still feels solid—not unlike the 9.4in iPad Pro I used to own. Like Dave, I could feel the crease at the centre point but not unpleasantly so, and it does serve as a very handy orientation point. For me, and accidental though this benefit may be, I preferred it to the iPad because of this. Sound as a Pound I was in a very busy Apple Store, so bear that in mind. Additionally, the only settings I changed were to enable BSI's quick activation gesture. I played no music and listened to no books. Nevertheless, I thought Daniel compact sounded very good, both in folded and unfolded landscape modes. Indeed, the latter reminded me of the beautiful audio that I used to get from the iPad Pro. I would therefore conclude that Apple must be doing something right with this. Was it any better than the audio from the iPhone 18 Pro, which I also tried? In unfolded landscape, I would say it was, though if you're in the market for a Pro and you have a 16 Pro Max like I do, I would immediately agree that the 18 Pro is a big step up from that, and worth it for the audio alone. Braille Screen Input I had really wanted to try this and I was blown away. In unfolded Landscape, the Duo was a breeze for BSI in tabletop mode. I tried typing as fast as the cable on the table would allow in a blank note in the notes app and made hardly any errors. Those I did make were down to the unfortunate stoop I had to adopt owing to the cable on the table aforesaid, compounded by Voiceover's being set to speak both characters and words—I had forgotten how utterly tiresome I find that much keyboard echo and how it appears to slow one down. I then folded the phone and tried it in Screen Away Mode. All I can say is the speed of my Landscape tabletop typing was blasted out of the water. Again, I tried to braille as fast as I could and I can't remember making any errors. Indeed, an Apple Store employee (a South African gentleman who rather unconvincingly assured me he wasn't sneakily checking the rugby score between Italy and South Africa whenever he could) witnessed the Bingo BSI masterclass, and I found I was able to dictate what I was writing at a perfectly natural speaking pace while still managing easily to keep up using BSI. In fact, this chap, who I will later explain was the kind of Apple employee who is honest rather than only interested in sales, said I typed comfortably quicker than he had seen sighted people do on the software keyboard. But it wasn't just about speed. The Duo, particularly in its folded state, is just the right shape for BSI. I find the Pro Max begins to tire my hands after a while as I have to hold it in position to input Braille. Not so with the Duo. I can't quite describe it, but everything seemed absolutely right in terms of shape, spacing, weight and balance. It was a pleasure. I can't put it more tangibly than that. A word on calibration: it appears that dot positions are calibrated on the Duo, folded or unfolded, in the same way as they are on most iPhones. That is to say, dots 4-5-6 followed by dots 1-2-3. If you have Voiceover hints enabled, Voiceover will tell you this is how to do it. I tried the 18 Pro way just to see if it worked. It doesn't. It's definitely the traditional way. The Tent, the Laptop and the Enormous Hand A quick word on other modes available. Unfolded Portrait is what Dave describes as like having a giant iPhone. Sorry, Dave, But that doesn't go far enough. Perhaps, and it is a big perhaps, Hagrid would find unfolded Portrait useful, but I cannot think who else would. I certainly did not and will say no more about it. The other two modes are Tent Mode and Laptop Mode. In Tent Mode, the Duo is in the classic tent shape i.e. halfway between folded and unfolded. The tent roof is composed half of the titanium back of the phone (which incidentally feels exquisite to hold), and half of the outer display. Laptop mode is simply the tent turned upside down. Half the inner display rests on the table. The other half is the lid of your laptop. What are they for? I'll leave it to our South African friend now that he knows South Africa are 45-0 up at half time, to do the honours of explaining: Tent Mode is if you want to watch movies. Laptop Mode is when you want to pretend you're a novelist. I'm with Dave on this one. No use for either. But I have no sight at all, and I'd be interested to hear from someone who tries Tent Mode to watch telly in particular. Trade-Offs and Compromises As Forgive me, folks, but as our South African friend is about to feature more in our story, I do wish I'd asked the poor fellow his name. Why didn't I? Alas I have no answer to that question. Anyway we started talking about trade-offs such as no Action Button. He confirmed that he had no idea why this was and that there was no official line on it, but thought it might be possible to use the Camera Control as a quasi-Action Button by reassigning it in settings. I know this can be done on the 16 Pro Max, but I can't recall to what extent and I did not try with the Duo today. Certainly, I don't think the Camera Control can be assigned to perform functions like switching to silent mode, which you can set the Action Button to do. by the way, the Camera Control looks very similar to the Side Button on the Duo, to the extent that I tried summoning Siri with the Camera Control by mistake on one occasion. In addition, there does not appear to be any old-style mute switch on the Duo, which I thought there might be given the absence of the Action Button. Our South African friend and I also discussed the absence of the LiDAR sensor. Now, I don't use Door Detection, People Detection or Point and Speak. I've just never found I wanted to, but if you do, you won't be able to use them in the same way. As our friend explained, LiDAR gives you distances, so the Duo won't be able to do that. However, we then tried VoiceOver's Scene Recognition with both the Duo and the iPhone 18 Pro to see what extra information the phone with the LiDAR sensor would give us, both phones obviously running Visual Intelligence. My honest opinion? There was so little difference between the two descriptions as to be of no account. Even our friend was quite surprised, though he went on very honestly to say that in his view, features like Door Detection are not as good as they have been in the past. For me, these features don't matter. If they matter to you, the Duo's not your bag. Our friend was also very forthcoming on durability and battery. The battery, said he, is up with the Pro in his experience if you use it folded most of the time. unfolded, you will obviously get less. To the extent that some people say you get a lot less, well all I can say (and our friend agreed with me) is that the novelty of being able to fold and unfold our diplomatic passport of a Duo means one's likely to do it rather a lot to begin with. It's a new toy, after all. Speaking of which, I've already mentioned that the hardware seems very, very robust. This was one of the issues on which I was most sceptical and my fears have been entirely assuaged. There is always AppleCare, but even without that readers should remember that in many countries including the UK, the US, Australia and all member states of the European Union, you also have your statutory consumer rights as to fitness for purpose on which to rely. Moreover, our friend told me that AppleCare for a Duo includes replacement of the layer that might get a little worn out or creased if it becomes unpleasant under the fingers in due course. Finally, our friend confirmed what I've always suspected: whereas he himself is a Face ID fan, he's finding that more people than he bargained for like Touch ID. That's great to know for fans of the fingerprint like myself. Why can't we have both, eh? Live and let live, I say. Our friend also confirmed that the Duo is selling very well, just behind the Pro Max, at Brent Cross—an interesting observation from what is a flagship London store. So it seems sighted people are prepared to make the camera trade-offs too. I found that surprising, but gratifying now I am a Duo man. Conclusions—Why I am Sold I love iPhones, and I lov iPads. This is both. It's presented in a genuine pocket-sized form factor, is a joy with BSI, feels and sounds great, and has Touch ID, which is not only convenient but also serves as an open invitation for those who get up specially early every morning to moan about blind Touch ID obsessives to launch a fresh crusade in the comments thread! As I explored the Duo, I imagined being able to unlock my phone on the Tube without dragging the iPhone out of my trouser pocket (it wen't fit the jacket) and waving it in front of my face. I imagined watching TV with those wonderful speakers in unfolded landscape and lovely speakers, it no longer mattering if I'd forgotten the portable Bluetooth one. I imagined easier games of chess and backgammon on a tablet-like screen. I imagined breaking off reading the newspaper in Easy Reader on the right hand side to send a quick WhatsApp message on the left, before returning to the paper, with the added bonus of knowing exactly where the splitter is. I have written this whole post on my 16 Pro Max, and by comparison it's somewhat cumbersome. Sure, there are trade-offs, and I have a great deal of sympathy with the argument that if you're paying as much as you are for the Duo, you should surely not have to compromise on anything. Additionally, some compromises such as the absence of an Action Button are difficult to fathom. Nevertheless, I'll live with the trade-offs. They are far outweighed by the attractions. I hope you've found this review, for want of a better word, helpful. I'm looking forward to reading other people's observations, and I don't just mean those of the Face ID merchants. Author's note: The pizzeria mentioned in the introduction to this article has pepperoni, bacon and mushroom, and cheeseburger pizzas as meat options. They are not deep pan but are decent Italian bases. The author can attest that they are an ideal snack en route out of the shopping centre. One slice will keep you going just fine.
